title: Accuracy Versus Precision Target Range
creator: Hank R. & Claude Code
subject: Environmental Monitoring
description: Drive bias and scatter as two independent sliders, produce all four quadrants of the accuracy-precision diagram yourself, and watch calibration fix exactly one of the two faults.

learningObjectives: Differentiate accuracy from precision by controlling bias and scatter independently.
Predict which fault a given sensor has.
Identify which fault calibration can repair.

keyQuestions: A sensor reads 25.1, 25.1, 25.0, 25.1 when the truth is 21. What is wrong with it, and can you fix it?
Why does averaging twenty readings not help a biased sensor?
Can an instrument be precise and useless at the same time?
commonMisconceptions: Believing more decimal places means a better measurement.
assessmentOpportunities: Predicts which fault a described sensor has before running it.
States that calibration repairs bias and cannot repair scatter.
Explains why averaging helps an imprecise sensor but not an inaccurate one.
